answer: One knoll is one forged identity. The shale is the one register anchoring every row, so clones must collide on it: a row keeps its entry only while it holds ferrous, iron drawn from a fixed circulating stock, and its iron decays each epoch and must be re-bought from the pool of decayed iron that every row bids for. So a thousand knolls bid against each other for one thin pool, and every extra clone makes each re-buy dearer; iron is never shared, so splitting buys nothing. It breaks if iron is minted on demand.
